test_title: PYST 9: Selection Post (Matric Level) - GA (Held On 01 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Where will India's Aditya-L1 mission be placed?

options.text: At the Sun-Earth L1 point in a halo orbit

solution:
The correct answer is __**At the Sun-Earth L1 point in a halo orbit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Aditya-L1** mission is **India’s first dedicated space mission** to study the **Sun**. It is designed to be placed in a **halo orbit** around the **Lagrangian point 1 (L1)** of the **Sun-Earth system**.
 
• The **Sun-Earth L1 point** is located approximately **1.5 million kilometers** away from the **Earth**, which is about **1%** of the total distance between the **Earth** and the **Sun**.
 
• A satellite placed in the **halo orbit** around the **L1 point** has the major advantage of continuously viewing the **Sun** without any **occultation** or **eclipses**. This allows for uninterrupted monitoring of **solar activities** and their impact on **space weather**.
 
• The **Lagrange points** are positions in space where the **gravitational forces** of a **two-body system** (like the Sun and Earth) produce enhanced regions of attraction and repulsion. These can be used by spacecraft to reduce **fuel consumption** needed to remain in position.
 
• Option 1 is incorrect because the **Sun-Earth L2 point** is located on the opposite side of the Earth from the Sun and is typically used for **space telescopes** like the **James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)** to observe the deep universe.
 
• Option 3 is incorrect because the **Earth-Moon L1 point** is located between the Earth and the Moon, which is not suitable for a mission dedicated to **solar observation**.
 
• Option 4 is incorrect because the **Mars-Sun L1 point** would be located near **Mars**, which is far beyond the scope of a mission intended to monitor the Sun from the vicinity of **Earth**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Launch Details:** The **Aditya-L1** spacecraft was successfully launched on **September 2, 2023**, by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** using the **PSLV-C57** launch vehicle from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre** in **Sriharikota**.
 
• **Mission Payloads:** The spacecraft carries **seven scientific payloads**. These include the **Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC)**, **Solar Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (SUIT)**, **Solar Low Energy X-ray Spectrometer (SoLEXS)**, **High Energy L1 Orbiting X-ray Spectrometer (HEL1OS)**, **Aditya Solar wind Particle Experiment (ASPEX)**, **Plasma Analyser Package For Aditya (PAPA)**, and **Advanced Tri-axial High Resolution Digital Magnetometers**.
 
• **Scientific Objectives:** The mission aims to study the **solar corona** (the outermost layer), **photosphere**, and **chromosphere**. It also investigates **Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs)**, **solar flares**, and the **solar wind** to understand the dynamics of the **solar atmosphere** and **coronal heating**.
 
• **Mission Duration:** The mission has a planned life of approximately **5.2 years**, during which it will provide crucial data to predict **space weather** events that can affect **satellite communications** and **power grids** on Earth.
 
• **Lagrange Points:** There are five such points in the **Sun-Earth system**, labeled **L1 to L5**. **L1**, **L2**, and **L3** are unstable, while **L4** and **L5** are stable points.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Halo Orbit:** Unlike a simple circular orbit, a **halo orbit** is a three-dimensional, periodic orbit near the **L1 point**. It allows the spacecraft to stay out of the **Earth's shadow** and maintain a constant line of sight with both the **Sun** and **Earth** ground stations.
 
• **Distance Comparison:** The distance to **L1** (**1.5 million km**) is much greater than the distance to the **International Space Station (ISS)**, which orbits at about **400 km**, but it is much less than the distance to the **Sun** (about **150 million km**).
 
• **Global Context:** With the success of **Aditya-L1**, **India** joins a select group of nations and agencies, such as **NASA** and the **ESA**, that have placed observatories at the **L1 point** for solar research, following missions like **SOHO (Solar and Heliospheric Observatory)**.
